source.title: What abliteration actually costs (and why KL won't tell you)

record.file_problem: The article is present; part of a footnote’s equation and surrounding text is garbled.
record.tranche_reason: Applies careful abliteration and measures its effects on truthful answering, a collateral ability not directly measured in the original refusal experiments.
record.gate_note: The post does not measure refusal rates, test refusal-direction addition, or directly test whether refusal is mediated by one direction. Its own results measure truthful answering and truth probes before and after careful abliteration, bearing on V1's claim that other abilities remain largely intact. Results cited from other work, including the 13-model TruthfulQA results and the later cone finding, are not recorded as rows. The ordinary-prompt KL value is not a measure of the outcomes named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post's own before/after measurements on four abliterated models (forced-choice and free-form TruthfulQA) bear on V1's clause that other abilities are largely kept. The post argues that KL-screened 'clean' abliteration hides a truthfulness cost, so this is a specific argument that V1 needs restating (T5) rather than a plain new setting. It does not measure refusal removal or induction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that careful, KL-screened abliteration leaves truth-probe accuracy intact but shifts output toward popular falsehoods in Qwen and Llama, and not in Yi or Gemma. The cost roughly triples in free-form generation for Qwen. KL screening cannot detect it. Which models pay, and why, is left open; they do not name the mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses careful, KL-screened abliteration based on the Arditi method; the post does not detail its full implementation. It investigates truthful-answering consequences rather than refusal removal or induction, and each model was abliterated once.
record.method_sensitivity: The truthful-answering effect varies by model: Qwen and Llama show declines, while Yi and Gemma do not show significant forced-choice declines; Gemma also shows no free-form increase. Forced-choice scoring variants differ in magnitude and significance, especially for Llama.

fits_no_version.finding: After careful abliteration, truth-probe accuracy stays essentially unchanged (0.873 vs 0.867) while truthful output drops on some models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration's collateral truthfulness cost is a shift in output disposition, not erasure of internally decodable truth knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: Ordinary-prompt KL of 0.034 certifies the edit as clean while the truthfulness cost is present.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KL-based screening of abliteration directions fails to detect collateral behavioural costs.

record.problems: The post reports one abliteration run per model and only four models on TruthfulQA. It does not save baseline refusal scores needed to assess safety-training as a predictor. The Gemma null conflicts with a cited result using a different, gameable metric. Free-form judges come from the same model family; reported agreement with human labels is κ = 0.61. Direct KL on the truth questions is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible own results omitted. Cited results and the ordinary-prompt KL value are excluded because they do not test a listed claim-version outcome.

untested.parts: Refusal removal by ablation, refusal induction by adding the direction, derivation and identity of the difference-in-means direction, and general capabilities beyond TruthfulQA.
No refusal rates after the weight edit are measured; only truthfulness side effects.
Not tested; the cone result is only cited.
Not tested; baseline refusal scores were not saved, so safety training could not be examined as a predictor.

missing.what: The post says probes 'hold' for Llama, Yi and Gemma, but gives no numbers; only Qwen's probe accuracy is reported.
Generation entropy of abliterated models is within a few percent of base, and answer distributions sharpen slightly. This is a control against an entropy explanation.

record.verdict_notes: Single abliteration run per model and four models only. Gemma's null conflicts with a cited gamed-metric result. The 13-model TruthfulQA table and the cone finding are cited work and are correctly excluded. The post does not verify refusal removal, so V1's core causal claim and V2 are not assessed; the verdicts concern only V1's 'other abilities kept' clause.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure refusal removal or induction, test the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, or assess general capabilities beyond the truthful-answering measures reported.
No refusal rate is measured after a practical weight edit.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is tested.
The post does not test whether refusal is affine, conical, or distributed across multiple directions; the cone result it mentions is cited work.
It studies truth representation and truthful answering, not harmfulness judgments versus refusal decisions.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer of the refusal direction is measured.
Model differences are reported, but refusal-training conditions are not controlled or tested.

relationships.condition: Qwen-27B (all forced-choice scorings, fluency-controlled margin, free-form generation)
relationships.reason: Qwen's truthful choice drops 3–5 points in all four scorings (r1–r4), and the drop survives surface controls (r17). Free-form falsehoods rise from 18.6% to 30.6% (r22) despite low KL.
relationships.display_finding: Truthful choice fell 3–5 points across all four scorings despite surface controls, and free-form falsehoods rose from 18.6% to 30.6% despite low KL.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B (three of four forced-choice scorings, margin, free-form)
relationships.reason: Llama shows smaller but significant drops in three scorings (r5–r7), a surface-robust margin shift (r18), and free-form falsehoods rising from 42.2% to 47.7% (r23). The fourth scoring is non-significant (r8).
relationships.display_finding: Llama-3.1-8B showed smaller significant declines in three scorings and a margin shift robust to surface controls, while free-form falsehoods rose from 42.2% to 47.7% and the fourth scoring showed no significant change.

relationships.condition: Yi-1.5-9B and Gemma-2-9B; Llama few-shot normalized cell
relationships.reason: Yi and Gemma show no significant forced-choice change (r9–r16, all p ≥ 0.20) and Gemma's free-form falsehood rate does not move (r24). Yi's margin intercept is non-significant (r19); Gemma's is faint (r20). Llama's few-shot normalized cell is also n.s. (r8).
relationships.display_finding: Yi and Gemma showed no significant forced-choice changes (all p ≥ 0.20), Gemma's free-form falsehood rate remained unchanged, and Llama's few-shot normalized result was also nonsignificant; Yi's margin intercept was nonsignificant and Gemma's was weak.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Truthful answering worsened after abliteration in the reported forced-choice and free-form settings, so the claim of preserved other abilities needs qualification; see r1-r8, r17-r18, and r22-r23.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Yi and Gemma forced-choice results; Gemma free-form result
reader_labels.reason: The post reports no significant forced-choice cost for Yi or Gemma and no free-form increase in Gemma; see r9-r16 and r24.
